summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop causing streaming timeouts and token latency spikes for Lexa Health
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Lexa Health reported sustained throughput degradation in their dedicated GPU pool beginning ~2026-03-10 09:15 UTC. Symptoms include streaming client disconnects, request timeouts (5–10s beyond normal), and per-token latency spikes from 60ms baseline to 400–1200ms on bursty jobs.

Impact:
- Affected customer: Lexa Health (dedicated tier).
- Service impact: increased error rates for streaming endpoints, consumer-facing delays in production features for multiple services using open-llama-13B and redwood-rlhf-2.1. Estimated 30% of calls in the pool timed out during peak window.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Cluster: dc-west-2a (6x A10G nodes at time of incident).
- Autoscaler config: target_utilization=0.78, scale_up_cooldown=120s, max_nodes=12.

Steps to reproduce (customer-side):
1) Submit 10 concurrent streaming chat sessions using open-llama-13B-q4 with 1.2k token prompts.
2) Observe observed latency and occasional client disconnects after 15s.
3) Re-run against a shared-hosted endpoint — no issue.

Observed metrics & logs:
- GPU utilization across nodes showed oscillating patterns: many nodes at 95–100% for short bursts while others at 10–30%.
- Per-instance p99 token latency correlated with spikes in GPU SM utilization and kernel queue length.
- Scheduler logs show several scale-up attempts throttled by resource fragmentation (no contiguous GPUs available for large allocations).
- cgroup oom events: none; memory pressure moderate.
- Network latency within cluster normal (infra-level p99 <1ms).
- Cloud provider reported transient MIG scheduling delays in the affected AZ between 09:00–10:00 UTC.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Support opened a temp capacity incident and provisioned 4 additional A10G nodes to Lexa Health pool at 09:45 UTC.
- Rebalanced tenant allocation to avoid packing large jobs on a single node; applied soft-affinity to spread heavy jobs.
- Increased autoscaler max_nodes from 12->18 as a temporary mitigation.

Current hypothesis:
- Combination of noisy-neighbor jobs that oversubscribe GPU SMs for short bursts plus suboptimal autoscaler packing/thresholds led to contention.
- Fragmentation of GPU allocation (topology-aware constraints) caused repeated small allocations to congest a subset of nodes, triggering high queueing latency.
- Cloud-side scheduling hiccups (provider-level MIG placement delays) amplified the effect during peak.

Next steps for investigation and remediation listed below in investigation_notes and follow_up_actions.

2026-03-10 09:40 - SRE (Owen Patel): Initial metrics show several nodes pegged at 100% GPU SM utilization while others low. Suspect packing/placement causing contention. Provisioning additional nodes now as a temporary relief.

2026-03-11 14:10 - SRE (Owen Patel): Investigation continues. Found scheduler packer was prioritizing bin-packing which increased GPU SM co-location of bursty jobs. Running a test build that prefers spread for dedicated pools to reduce burst contention.
2026-03-12 10:15 - Support (Maya Chen): Applied scheduler config change to prefer spread for this dedicated pool (rollout PR merged: runtime/pull/2987). Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Lexa Health (Elena@lexa): Observed stable latency over past 3 hours; no disconnects. Will continue to monitor during peak. Thank you.
2026-03-12 17:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Moving issue to In Progress -> awaiting validation window. Planning follow-up capacity sizing review with customer and a runbook update.
investigation_notes: 09:30: GPU SM utilization heatmap indicates bursty saturation on subset of nodes correlated with customer job timestamps.
09:34: Scheduler logs: multiple failed attempts to place large allocation due to fragmentation; fallback packing into partially-used nodes observed.
09:50: Cloud provider status: reported transient MIG scheduling latency in AZ which increased allocation delays for 6 minutes.
Test run: changing packer policy from aggressive bin-pack to topology-aware spread reduced p99 token latency from ~900ms to ~120ms in internal simulation for identical load.
No evidence of memory OOM or network congestion; root cause points to GPU kernel queueing and scheduling contention (noisy neighbor effect).
resolution: Temporary: provisioned 4 additional A10G nodes to Lexa Health pool and increased autoscaler cap to 18 nodes to reduce immediate contention.
Medium-term: changed scheduler packing policy for dedicated pools to prefer spread for latency-sensitive tenants (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2987).
Long-term: plan to add per-tenant burst isolation and recommend per-tenant GPU reservation profiles to customers with bursty workloads.
Customer validated improvement on 2026-03-12; no further timeouts reported during validation window.
